s1a: One customer calls. One writes. One goes to PayPal.
s1b: What the shop does next decides what it costs.
s2a: A PayPal dispute answered early costs no fee. Lost as a claim, fourteen euros. For a busy shop, twenty-eight, even when it wins.
s2b: Every customer-care contact costs about eight dollars.
s2c: Every dollar lost to fraud costs about four dollars sixty.
s2d: And big merchants give up on almost half of their card chargebacks.
s3a: That's where Second Look comes in. Every request, by phone, email, form or PayPal, lands in one place.
s3b: Second Look finds its order. Second Look's AI checks the evidence and drafts the answer. Your limits, written in code, have the last word.
s3c: A person approves, and everything is updated: the reply, PayPal, the helpdesk, the accounts.
s4a: Meet Linen and Paper, a made-up shop with about two thousand orders a month.
s4b: Marta, a customer care assistant, can give back up to thirty euros. Giulia, head of customer care, decides above that.
s5a: Giulia's morning starts here: everything that came in, every channel, beside the day's orders.
s5b: Each request already matched to its order and checked by Second Look's AI. And who has what.
s5c: And the routine ones? After ten approved unchanged, Giulia let Second Look's AI answer them alone. It signs what it sends, and steps back when it isn't sure.
s6a: Sophie, a customer, called Marta: her tablecloth never arrived. The call is transcribed on the shop's own computer, and her email joins it. One case.
s6b: The courier left it with a neighbour. Marta sends the reply and closes the case: solved before any dispute.
s7a: Dario, a customer, opened a PayPal dispute. In Marta's helpdesk, Second Look's AI says: defend.
s7b: It was delivered to his PayPal address, and he has disputed four of his five orders.
s7c: Refunding now would cost twenty-six euros. Marta defends: the proof goes to PayPal.
s8a: Pablo, a customer, emailed, then opened a PayPal dispute. Still one case.
s8b: He's right: his returned shirt was never refunded. Eighty-nine euros is over Marta's limit, so Giulia approves it.
s9a: And at the end of the month, Giulia knows: requests, how many were solved before a dispute, staff time, money back and fees.
s9b: The accounts get every refund as it happens.
s10a: And it runs on PayPal. On PayPal's sandbox, a real dispute got its reply and proof, and Second Look refunded a payment through PayPal's own refund API.
s11a: Second Look's AI recommends. Your limits have the last word. You approve.
